model_call_location: The model is called in the host only — src/mcp_agent.py run() -> tracing.call_model (Groq) — between tools/list and tools/call; it never happens on this wire or inside either MCP server.
captured_with: python week9/capture_wire.py (raw newline-delimited JSON-RPC over the server's stdin/stdout, no SDK client); verbatim bytes in week9/wire_raw.json
server: claims-system (mcp_servers/claims_system_server.py), launched as configured in mcp_config.json

annotations.jsonrpc: Always the literal '2.0'. MCP rides on JSON-RPC 2.0; a message without it is not valid on this wire.
annotations.id: 1 — the client picks it. The response must carry the same id; that is how a reply is matched to its request over one stdio pipe.
annotations.method: 'initialize' — must be the first request. Nothing else is legal until the handshake is done.
annotations.params.protocolVersion: The newest spec version the CLIENT speaks (2026-07-28, from the SDK). It is an offer, not a demand.
annotations.params.capabilities: Empty: this client offers no sampling, roots or elicitation, so the server can never ask the host to run a model or show the user anything.
annotations.params.clientInfo: Name/version of the caller. Informational only — it is NOT authentication; anyone can claim any name here.

exchange.raw: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"capabilities":{"prompts":{"listChanged":false},"resources":{"listChanged":false,"subscribe":false},"tools":{"listChanged":false}},"instructions":"Claim records and adjuster note history from the claims platform.","protocolVersion":"2025-11-25","serverInfo":{"name":"claims-system","version":""}}}

annotations.id: 1 — echoes the request id, so this answers the initialize above.
annotations.result.protocolVersion: 2025-11-25 — the server did NOT accept 2026-07-28; it answered with the newest version it supports. Negotiation result: the session runs on 2025-11-25. A client that cannot speak it must disconnect.
annotations.result.capabilities: What the server offers: tools, resources and prompts, all with listChanged=false (the tool list will not change mid-session, so one tools/list is enough). No 'sampling' anywhere — there is no model on this side.
annotations.result.instructions: Free text the host MAY put into the model's context. Third-party text: it is a prompt-injection surface, which is why mcp_agent.py does not forward it.
annotations.result.serverInfo: name 'claims-system', version '' — the server does not even declare a version, so the host cannot pin or audit which build it is talking to (risk note).

annotations.(no id): No id = a NOTIFICATION: fire and forget, the server sends no reply. That is why the capture shows no response line here.
annotations.method: 'notifications/initialized' — the client confirms it accepted the negotiated version. Only after this is the session open for tools/list and tools/call.
'tools/list' — discovery. This is the call that makes adding a server a config change: the host learns the tools from here, not from its own code.
annotations.params: Empty: no cursor, so the first (and here only) page.

exchange.raw:
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"result":{"tools":[{"description":"Return the claim record filed under one claim number: workflow status,
policy forms in force, date of loss, amount claimed and the excess on file.
Does not return adjuster notes or policy wording.","inputSchema":{"properties":{"claim_number":{"title":"Claim Number","type":"string"}},"required":["claim_number"],"type":"object","title":"get_claim_statusArguments"},"name":"get_claim_status"},{"description":"Return the adjuster note history for one claim number, oldest first.
An empty history means no adjuster has inspected the claim yet.","inputSchema":{"properties":{"claim_number":{"title":"Claim Number","type":"string"}},"required":["claim_number"],"type":"object","title":"get_adjuster_notesArguments"},"name":"get_adjuster_notes"}]}}

annotations.result.tools: Two tools. Each entry has exactly three fields the host uses:
annotations.result.tools[].name: The identifier the model will emit in a tool call (get_claim_status, get_adjuster_notes).
annotations.result.tools[].description: The tool's docstring, verbatim. This text goes straight into the model's prompt — it IS a prompt, written by the server's author, not by us.
annotations.result.tools[].inputSchema: JSON Schema for the arguments, generated from the Python type hints. The host passes it to the model unchanged as the function 'parameters'.

annotations.method: 'tools/call' — run one tool. In the agent this is sent by the HOST after the model asked for it; the model never talks to the server.
annotations.params.name: 'get_claim_status' — must match a name from tools/list.
annotations.params.arguments: {'claim_number': 'CLM-2024-60337'} — validated by the server against the inputSchema before the function runs.

annotations.result.content: A list of content blocks. One block, type 'text', holding the claim record as a JSON string. The host joins the text blocks and hands them to the model as the tool message.
annotations.result.isError: false. A failed tool call is NOT a JSON-RPC error: it comes back as a normal result with isError=true and the message in content, so the MODEL can read it and recover (e.g. the claim-number-format error). A JSON-RPC 'error' object would be a protocol failure the model never sees.
